source.title: The influence of the stiffness of GelMA substrate on the outgrowth of PC12 cells

formulation.evidence: To form GelMA hydrogels with different concentrations (5, 10, 20, and 30%)
The photoinitiator (Irgacure 2959) was then added to the precursor solutions at a concentration of 0.5% (w/v).

processing.evidence: the solutions were exposed to a UV light with 1.5 mW/cm2 intensity and 365 nm wavelength for photocrosslinking of 30 s
the solutions were exposed to a UV light with 1.5 mW/cm2 intensity and 365 nm wavelength for photocrosslinking of 30 s

youngs_modulus.evidence: The 10% of GelMA hydrogels were much stiffer with the Young's modulus of 34.9 KPa

culture_days.evidence: After incubation for 24, 72, and 120 h, the cell-seeded hydrogel disks were rinsed with PBS

viability_percent.evidence: cell viability of all groups at 24–120 h was approximately 95%, showing no significant difference

neurite_length.evidence: After incubating for 24h, PC12 cell shows the longest neurite length on 10% GelMA substrates with 34.9 KPa, which was 49.9 μm

survival.evidence: cell viability of all groups at 24–120 h was approximately 95%, showing no significant difference

notes: Uniaxial tensile test at room temperature. Identified as optimal for PC12 neurite outgrowth and spreading.
